messages:
alex_dev: Quick Q: Node fetch + Basic auth — what should I base64 encode for our API key? I'm doing `Authorization: Basic ${Buffer.from(apiKey).toString('base64')}` but some examples add a trailing colon. GH Actions secret is acting weird too.
maria: Always include the colon. Basic auth is username:password base64. For token-only API keys the server expects `base64(apiKey + ':')` so do `Buffer.from(`${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}:`).toString('base64')`.
kevin: Also be careful with quoting in .env and CI: if your secret has a trailing newline it will change the base64. In GH Actions avoid newline when saving a secret or use `echo -n` in your workflow when you write it out.
jules: Node-fetch example that works: `fetch(url, { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(`${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}:`).toString('base64') }})` — and no, don't URL-encode the colon.
alex_dev: Ah — thanks. And if the key is used alone (no password) still include the colon even if server ignores password?
maria: :thumbsup: Yep. Server decodes and splits on `:`. Without colon some auth parsers treat the entire decoded string as username and then expect a password field; including the colon avoids that ambiguity.
kevin: curl example for reference: `curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"$REDWOOD_API_KEY:\" | base64)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/...`
jules: Windows gotcha: `echo -n` isn't available in cmd. Use `printf '%s' "$KEY:" | base64` or PowerShell: `Write-Output -NoNewline $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY; "|" | base64` (or use the SDK).
devx-bot: FYI: Our official SDKs will set the Authorization header for you if you initialize the client with the api key. Using the SDK avoids these small header/encoding bugs.
alex_dev: Good call — switching to the SDK. Thanks y'all :pray:
